# Understanding how a changing world reshapes disease.

PACE Lab connects animal movement, ecological change, and quantitative modeling to understand pathogen transmission—and to strengthen wildlife conservation, animal health, and One Health preparedness.

[Our approach](#our-approach){.btn .btn-primary} [Meet the lab](people.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}
:::
:::

::: {.page-shell}
::: {.intro-grid}
::: {}
## About PACE Lab

PACE Lab investigates **P**athogen transmission through **A**nimal movement, environmental **C**hanges, and **E**cological community dynamics.

We combine quantitative analysis with mechanistic modeling—particularly individual-based and network models—alongside statistical models and machine learning to understand infectious-disease ecology and transmission across scales.
:::

::: {.focus-note}
### Current focus

Our work focuses especially on migratory birds and avian influenza, including how climate and landscape changes affect:

- host movement and community composition
- wildlife–poultry–human interfaces
- transmission, spillover, and viral evolution
:::
:::

## Our approach {#our-approach}

::: {.approach-grid}
::: {.approach-card}
### Link ecology and disease

We study how movement, environmental change, and host communities shape when and where pathogens spread.
:::

::: {.approach-card}
### Build quantitative models

We use mechanistic, network, epidemiological, statistical, and machine-learning approaches to connect ecological data with prediction.
:::

::: {.approach-card}
### Support action

We aim to generate knowledge that supports wildlife conservation, animal health, and preparedness at the wildlife–poultry–human interface.
:::
:::
